content.Tirofiban: Bolus 25 mcg/kg i.v. over 3 min followed by infusion 0.15 mcg/kg/min for up to 18 h. For CrCl <60 mL/min: LD 25 mcg/kg i.v. over 5 min followed by maintenance infusion 0.075 mcg/kg/min continued for up to 18 h. Contraindications: prior intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), ischaemic stroke within 30 days, recent fibrinolysis, or platelet count <100,000/mm3.

Anticoagulant drugs.UFH: Initial: i.v. bolus 70–100 U/kg followed by i.v. infusion titrated to achieve an aPTT of ~60–80 s. During PCI: 70–100 U/kg i.v. bolus or per ACT if UFH pre-treatment.
Anticoagulant drugs.Enoxaparin: Initial for ACS: 1 mg/kg b.i.d. subcutaneously for a minimum of 2 days and continued until clinical stabilization. If CrCl <30 mL/min (Cockcroft–Gault) reduce to 1 mg/kg o.d. During PCI: if last s.c. dose <8 h before balloon inflation no additional dosing; if >8 h before, give i.v. bolus 0.3 mg/kg enoxaparin sodium.
Anticoagulant drugs.Bivalirudin: During PPCI: 0.75 mg/kg i.v. bolus followed by i.v. infusion 1.75 mg/kg/h for 4 h after procedure. If CrCl <30 mL/min, reduce maintenance infusion to 1 mg/kg/h.
Anticoagulant drugs.Fondaparinux: Initial: 2.5 mg/d subcutaneously. During PCI: a single bolus of UFH is recommended. Avoid if CrCl <20 mL/min.

Antiplatelet drugs.Aspirin: Loading dose (LD) 150–300 mg orally or 75–250 mg i.v. if oral ingestion not possible, followed by oral maintenance dose (MD) 75–100 mg o.d.; no specific dose adjustment in CKD patients.
Antiplatelet drugs.P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (oral or i.v.): Listed as the class of antiplatelet agents to be used (heading present); specific agents and dosing not shown on this page image.
